fields.Volume: ~15 departments × ~30 expense line items = ~450 data points

workflows.name: Monthly Department Expense Budget vs. Actual Tracking

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "generates monthly expense budget vs." (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews departmental expense reports" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "Department heads review their expense reports" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-345 (ensure controlled execution — Expense Monitoring & Control (PA-34.3).)
- operational: FP&A review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Explain-away culture**: variances are explained monthly but never corrected; mitigated by corrective-action confirmation and CFO follow-through at the operating review (steps 3–4)
- **Phasing blindness**: full-month budgets hide intra-month burn rates; mitigated by YTD actual-vs-budget phasing in the standard report (step 1)
System Touchpoints: - Monthly expense budget-vs-actual report per department by Day 3, monthly and YTD (step 1)
- Variance flagging — > 5% of monthly budget or > PHP 100K (step 2)
- Corrective action confirmation by department heads (step 3)
- CFO consolidated review at the monthly operating review (W1653) (step 4)
Time Estimate: Monthly cycle ~17 hours (FP&A variance review 2 hours + department-head expense reviews 1 hour × ~15 departments) ≈ 200 hours/year across ~450 expense data points (report generation automated); consolidated CFO review rides W1653.

steps.activity: System generates monthly expense budget vs. actual report per department by Day 3: (a) actual spend by expense category vs. monthly budget and YTD budget, (b) variance amount and %, (c) forecast for remaining months (based on run rate and known commitments)

FP&A reviews departmental expense reports: (a) flags variances > 5% of monthly budget or > PHP 100K, (b) identifies root cause categories (one-time vs. recurring), (c) assesses YTD implications for full-year budget
Department heads review their expense reports: (a) explain significant variances to FP&A, (b) identify corrective actions if over budget, (c) confirm or adjust remaining year forecast
CFO reviews consolidated expense performance at monthly operating review (W1653): (a) total OpEx vs. budget, (b) department-level highlights, (c) action items for over-budget departments

fields.Participants: VP Store Operations, Regional Managers, Store Managers, Finance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-calculate of "calculates monthly controllable expense KPIs per store" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-identify of "identify top 10 and bottom 10 stores by controllable expense ratio" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "review specific expense categories driving high costs" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-345 (ensure controlled execution — Expense Monitoring & Control (PA-34.3).)
- operational: VP Store Operations review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Apples-to-oranges benchmarking**: format and size differences distort store comparisons; mitigated by cluster-average benchmarking of similar stores (step 2)
- **Cost-cut-into-experience risk**: expense pressure degrades service and store standards; mitigated by pairing expense KPIs with the operational/customer KPIs on the W1655 scorecard (step 1)
System Touchpoints: - Store controllable-expense KPIs — utilities per sqm, maintenance % of revenue, supplies per store (step 1)
- Cluster benchmarking — each store vs. similar-format cluster average and chain average (step 2)
- Bottom-10 coaching loop with root-cause category analysis (step 3)
- Top-10 best-practice sharing through Regional Managers (step 4)
Time Estimate: Monthly cycle ~6–8 hours (cluster benchmarking 2 hours + bottom-10 store coaching 30 min/store + best-practice communication 1 hour) ≈ 72–96 hours/year (controllable-expense KPI calculation automated).

steps.activity: System calculates monthly controllable expense KPIs per store: (a) utilities per sqm (electricity, water), (b) maintenance cost as % of revenue, (c) supplies cost per transaction, (d) shrinkage as % of revenue, (e) overtime cost as % of payroll, (f) total controllable expense as % of revenue

VP Store Operations benchmarks stores: (a) compare each store to cluster average (stores of similar size and format), (b) compare each store to chain average, (c) identify top 10 and bottom 10 stores by controllable expense ratio, (d) trend analysis (improving vs. declining)

Regional Manager coaches bottom 10 stores: (a) review specific expense categories driving high costs, (b) identify root causes (e.g., high electricity → aging aircon units; high maintenance → deferred maintenance), (c) agree on action plans with Store Managers
Best practice sharing: VP Store Operations communicates expense management practices from top 10 performing stores to bottom 10 through regional manager network

fields.Frequency: Monthly statement reconciliation; ongoing compliance monitoring
fields.Trigger: Corporate credit card program for authorized personnel
fields.Volume: ~50–80 corporate cards issued (C-Suite, department heads, regional managers, selected store managers)

workflows.name: Company Expense Card & Corporate Credit Card Management

Automation Opportunity: - System rule-based authorization of "Corporate card issuance" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-submit of "submit reconciled statement to Finance by 5th of month" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Finance reviews reconciliation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: Finance — Treasury review and approval gate; periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Personal-expense commingling**: personal charges ride the corporate card; mitigated by receipt-level reconciliation with violation monitoring (steps 2–3)
- **Orphan-card risk**: cards remain active for departed employees; mitigated by the issuance register tied to the separation process (W43) (step 1)
System Touchpoints: - Card issuance register — authorized positions only (C-Suite, VPs, dept heads, RMs, selected Store Managers) (step 1)
- Monthly statement reconciliation with receipts matched to expense/budget codes (step 2)
- Policy-violation checks — personal expenses, unauthorized merchants, excessive amounts (step 3)
- Quarterly usage audit — compliance rate, violation rate, spend analytics (step 4)
Time Estimate: Cardholder statement reconciliation 30 min/cardholder/month × ~50–80 corporate cards ≈ 300–480 hours/year; Finance reconciliation review 4 hours/month ≈ 48 hours/year; quarterly usage audit 4 hours ≈ 16 hours/year; card issuance per authorized-position event.

steps.activity: Corporate card issuance: (a) authorized positions: C-Suite, VP-level, department heads, regional managers, selected store managers (for emergency purchases), (b) credit limit per card tier: Executive (PHP 500K), Department Head (PHP 200K), Regional Manager (PHP 100K), Store Manager (PHP 50K), (c) cardholder signs cardholder agreement with usage policy

Monthly: cardholder reconciles statement: (a) match each transaction to expense category and budget code, (b) attach receipts/invoices for all transactions > PHP 1,000, (c) submit reconciled statement to Finance by 5th of month

Finance reviews reconciliation: (a) verify receipts attached, (b) check for policy violations (personal expenses, unauthorized merchants, excessive amounts), (c) process payment (auto-debit from corporate bank account)
Quarterly: Finance audits corporate card usage: (a) compliance rate (receipts provided ÷ total transactions), (b) policy violation rate, (c) average spend per card, (d) unusual patterns

fields.Trigger: Employee business travel or entertainment event

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-create of "creates travel request in system" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews and approves" (replaces manual Step 3).
- System auto-validate of "verify compliance with policy" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - operational: HR / Finance review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Retro-authorization risk**: trips taken first and expensed after, defeating pre-approval; mitigated by the authorization-before-travel requirement (step 1)
- **Per-diem padding**: claimed days exceed approved travel days; mitigated by days × rate calculation verified against the approved travel dates (steps 3–4)
System Touchpoints: - Travel authorization workflow — approval before travel (< PHP 20K supervisor; higher tiers above) (step 1)
- Per-diem standard — PHP 1,500/day domestic; hotel at actuals within caps (step 2)
- 5-business-day post-travel expense report submission (step 3)
- Reimbursement processing with BIR-documentation-compliant reporting (step 4)
Time Estimate: ~70 min per travel/entertainment cycle (travel authorization 30 min + post-travel expense report 30 min + Finance reimbursement processing 10 min) × ~200–300 reports/month ≈ 2,800–4,200 hours/year (per-diem rates per policy).

steps.activity: Travel authorization: (a) employee creates travel request in system: destination, dates, purpose, estimated cost, (b) approval: < PHP 20K by direct supervisor; < PHP 50K by department head; > PHP 50K by VP, (c) travel booking: through designated travel agency or approved booking platform (for cost control)

Per diem and reimbursement rates (Philippine standard): (a) domestic travel per diem: PHP 1,500/day (covers meals and incidentals), (b) hotel: actual cost up to tier limit (Executive: PHP 5K/night; Manager: PHP 3K/night; Staff: PHP 2K/night), (c) transportation: economy class for domestic flights; business class for international only with VP approval; local transport: taxi/Grab with receipts

Post-travel: employee submits expense report within 5 business days: (a) itemized expenses with receipts, (b) per diem calculation (days × rate), (c) actual vs. pre-approved budget comparison, (d) approver reviews and approves

Finance processes reimbursement: (a) verify compliance with policy, (b) deduct advances if any, (c) reimburse via payroll or separate bank transfer, (d) GL posting to correct department and expense category

fields.Frequency: Monthly bill review; quarterly energy optimization review
fields.Participants: Facilities Manager, VP Store Operations, Store Managers, Finance
fields.Volume: 200 stores + 4 DCs + HQ = ~205 utility accounts (electricity); ~205 water accounts

workflows.name: Utility Expense Monitoring & Energy Cost Optimization

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-record of "records bill amount per location per month" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "monitors utility KPIs" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-measure of "measures" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-345 (ensure controlled execution — Expense Monitoring & Control (PA-34.3).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Bill-error leakage**: tariff misclassifications and estimated reads overcharge utilities; mitigated by monthly bill processing with KPI anomaly flags (steps 1–2)
- **Efficiency-deferral risk**: high-ROI optimization deferred indefinitely; mitigated by the annual investment evaluation quantifying payback on the total spend (step 4)
System Touchpoints: - Utility bill processing — Meralco, Davao Light, VECO and regional utilities for 200 stores + 4 DCs (step 1)
- Utility KPI monitoring — electricity PHP 80–120/sqm/month benchmark, water, waste (step 2)
- Energy optimization register — LED retrofit (~18-month ROI), aircon standardization (step 3)
- Annual optimization investment evaluation against ~PHP 300–500M/year utility spend (step 4)
Time Estimate: Monthly utility cycle ~20 hours (bill processing across ~410 utility accounts 2 days + KPI monitoring 4 hours) ≈ 240 hours/year; annual energy-optimization investment evaluation 1 week ≈ 40 hours/year; quarterly optimization review.

steps.activity: Monthly: Finance processes utility bills: (a) electricity bills from Meralco (Metro Manila/Luzon), Davao Light (Mindanao), VECO (Cebu), and other regional electric cooperatives, (b) water bills from local water districts, (c) system records bill amount per location per month

Facilities Manager monitors utility KPIs: (a) electricity cost per sqm per month (benchmark: PHP 80–120/sqm/month for warehouse retail), (b) water cost per sqm per month, (c) trend analysis: month-over-month and year-over-year, (d) flags locations with > 20% increase vs. same month prior year

Energy optimization opportunities: (a) LED lighting retrofit (stores still using fluorescent — ROI ~18 months), (b) aircon temperature standardization (set at 24–25°C per DOE recommendation), (c) motion-sensor lighting in backroom/warehouse areas, (d) solar panel installation for stores with large roof area (Philippine solar viability is high — ROI ~4–5 years), (e) generator fuel optimization per W808

Annual: Facilities Manager and Finance evaluate energy optimization investments: (a) total utility spend (~PHP 300–500M/year for 200 stores + 4 DCs), (b) savings from implemented measures, (c) proposed new investments with ROI analysis, (d) present to CFO for capex budget inclusion

fields.Frequency: Daily disbursements; bi-weekly or monthly replenishment
fields.Trigger: Petty cash disbursement or replenishment request
fields.Volume: 200 stores × PHP 20K float + 4 DCs × PHP 50K float = PHP 4.2M total petty cash

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Petty cash disbursement" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews receipts for compliance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "documented and investigated" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-345 (ensure controlled execution — Expense Monitoring & Control (PA-34.3).)
- operational: Store Manager (store); DC Supervisor (DC) review and approval gate; periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Float-drain risk**: un-replenished float halts small operational purchases; mitigated by the 30%-threshold replenishment trigger (step 2)
- **Count-variance risk**: physical-vs-expected mismatch signals leakage; mitigated by the monthly count with Finance sign-off and variance investigation (step 3)
System Touchpoints: - Petty cash disbursement control — < PHP 5K per transaction per FIN-017, larger via requisition (step 1)
- Float replenishment at 30% threshold with receipt substantiation (step 2)
- Monthly physical count vs. system-expected balance reconciliation (step 3)
Time Estimate: Disbursement handling 5 min/transaction at realized petty-cash volume; replenishment processing 30 min per cycle (bi-weekly to monthly per location); monthly reconciliation 30 min/location × ~205 locations ≈ 1,230 hours/year (205 × 0.5 h × 12) on PHP 4.2M total float.

steps.activity: Petty cash disbursement (per FIN-017): (a) employee requests petty cash for small expense (< PHP 5K per transaction; > PHP 5K requires purchase requisition per W1675), (b) Store Manager or DC Supervisor approves and disburses cash, (c) employee provides receipt within 3 business days, (d) custodian records transaction in petty cash log

Petty cash replenishment: (a) when float drops below 30% (PHP 6K for stores; PHP 15K for DCs), custodian submits replenishment request with all receipts attached, (b) Finance reviews receipts for compliance, (c) approves replenishment, (d) fund transfer or cash delivery via CIT service per FIN-025

Monthly reconciliation: (a) custodian counts physical cash on hand, (b) system calculates expected balance (float − disbursements + replenishments), (c) variance documented and investigated, (d) > PHP 500 variance requires Store Manager explanation, (e) Finance audits random sample of 10 stores per month for petty cash compliance

fields.Participants: Internal Audit, Finance, department heads, Loss Prevention
fields.Trigger: Monthly compliance monitoring cycle; quarterly internal audit

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-submit of "submitted late" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "documentation requirements, and policy limits" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalated to CFO and CEO" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-345 (ensure controlled execution — Expense Monitoring & Control (PA-34.3).)
- operational: Internal Audit review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Repeat-finding tolerance**: the same violations recur each quarter without consequence; mitigated by escalation of repeat findings to CFO and CEO (step 3)
- **Sample-miss risk**: a small audit sample misses systematic abuse; mitigated by full-population monthly monitoring layered under the sampled quarterly audit (steps 1–2)
System Touchpoints: - Monthly compliance monitoring — unapproved transactions, over-budget without override (step 1)
- Quarterly Internal Audit expense audit — 50–100 transaction sample against approval thresholds (step 2)
- Findings tracking to closure with escalation for repeats (step 3)
- Annual expense policy update from audit findings and tax-rule changes (step 4)
Time Estimate: Monthly compliance monitoring 4 hours ≈ 48 hours/year across ~1,500–2,000 expense transactions/month; quarterly Internal Audit sample of 50–100 transactions 1 week/quarter ≈ 32 hours/year; annual policy refresh 1 week ≈ 40 hours/year; corrective-action tracking ongoing.

steps.activity: Monthly: Finance monitors expense policy compliance: (a) transactions without proper approval, (b) transactions exceeding budget without override approval, (c) duplicate expense claims, (d) expense reports submitted late (> 5 business days after travel), (e) missing receipts on corporate card transactions, (f) petty cash transactions exceeding PHP 5K limit

Quarterly: Internal Audit conducts expense audit: (a) sample 50–100 expense transactions across departments, (b) verify compliance with approval thresholds, documentation requirements, and policy limits, (c) test petty cash at 10 random stores, (d) test corporate card transactions for 10 cardholders, (e) report findings with severity rating and corrective actions
Findings communicated to department heads; corrective actions tracked to closure; repeat findings escalated to CFO and CEO

Annual: Finance reviews and updates expense policy based on: (a) audit findings and common compliance gaps, (b) changes in Philippine tax regulations (BIR requirements for deductible expenses), (c) organizational changes (new roles, new locations), (d) communicate policy updates to all employees
